# Josie Pye

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c23 P5](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0005), [v1 c23 P12](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0012), [v1 c23 P41](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0041)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea  <sub>[v1 c34 P17](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0017), [v1 c34 P19](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0019)</sub>
- **Role:** Student  <sub>[v1 c34 P19](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0019), [v1 c37 P34](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0034)</sub>

## Appearance

She is a member of the Pye family.

_Sources: [v1 c37 P33](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0033)_

## Personality

Josie is known for her aggravating, disagreeable nature, lack of tact, and inclination to crow over others. She displays a competitive and defiant disposition, frequently challenging her peers to dares. Her lack of imagination causes her to dislike creative activities such as school recitations.

_Sources: [v1 c23 P5](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0005), [v1 c23 P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006), [v1 c23 P11](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0011), [v1 c23 P41](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0041), [v1 c34 P19](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0019), [v1 c37 P32](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0032), [v1 c37 P33](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0033)_

## Traits

- Aggravating  <sub>[v1 c34 P19](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0019)</sub>
- Disagreeable  <sub>[v1 c37 P33](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0033)</sub>
- Defiant  <sub>[v1 c23 P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006), [v1 c23 P11](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0011)</sub>
- Competitive  <sub>[v1 c23 P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006), [v1 c23 P11](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0011)</sub>
- Lacks imagination  <sub>[v1 c23 P41](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0041)</sub>

## Abilities

- Natural gift for walking board fences  <sub>[v1 c23 P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006)</sub>

## History

Josie grew up in Avonlea as a classmate of Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, Jane Andrews, and Ruby Gillis. During a garden party at Diana's house, she excelled at walking a board fence after daring Jane Andrews to hop on one leg. When Anne belittled the accomplishment, Josie dared Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's kitchen roof, resulting in Anne falling and breaking her ankle. She later visited the injured Anne at Green Gables, though her presence was attributed partly to remorse. Josie attended Queen's Academy alongside her Avonlea peers to pursue her studies, boarding in town and boasting about its superiority over Avonlea. After finishing her initial year at Queen's, she planned to return for further study rather than taking a teaching position.

_Sources: [v1 c23 P5](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0005), [v1 c23 P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006), [v1 c23 P11](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0011), [v1 c23 P15](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0015), [v1 c23 P41](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0041), [v1 c34 P19](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0019), [v1 c37 P34](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0034)_

- Belongs to the Pye family of Avonlea  <sub>[v1 c34 P17](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0017), [v1 c37 P33](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0033)</sub>

## Quotes

> I don’t believe anybody could walk a ridgepole. You couldn’t, anyhow.  <sub>[v1 c23 P9](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0009)</sub>

> Then I dare you to do it. I dare you to climb up there and walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry’s kitchen roof.  <sub>[v1 c23 P11](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0011)</sub>

> You’ve been crying. I suppose you’re homesick—some people have so little self-control in that respect. I’ve no intention of being homesick, I can tell you. Town’s too jolly after that poky old Avonlea. I wonder how I ever existed there so long. You shouldn’t cry, Anne; it isn’t becoming, for your nose and eyes get red, and then you seem all red. I’d a perfectly scrumptious time in the Academy today. Our French professor is simply a duck. His moustache would give you kerwollowps of the heart. Have you anything eatable around, Anne? I’m literally starving. Ah, I guessed likely Marilla ‘d load you up with cake. That’s why I called round. Otherwise I’d have gone to the park to hear the band play with Frank Stockley. He boards same place as I do, and he’s a sport. He noticed you in class today, and asked me who the red-headed girl was. I told him you were an orphan that the Cuthberts had adopted, and nobody knew very much about what you’d been before that.  <sub>[v1 c34 P19](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0019)</sub>

> Queen’s is to get one of the Avery scholarships after all. The word came today. Frank Stockley told me—his uncle is one of the board of governors, you know. It will be announced in the Academy tomorrow.  <sub>[v1 c34 P24](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0024)</sub>
